artillery_problem: Stone curtain walls shattered under repeated direct fire
defensive_response: Back walls with deep earth that absorbed and dispersed impact
operational_effect: Bombardment had to move more material before opening an assaultable breach
evidence: Peter Lorge and Geoffrey Parker describe low thick earth-backed artillery fortifications as the defensive answer to cannon.
limits: Design logic does not supply a universal wall thickness or breach time.

artillery_problem: Tall medieval walls offered conspicuous vertical targets
defensive_response: Lower the defensive silhouette and sink works behind ditches and slopes
operational_effect: Direct fire saw less exposed masonry while attackers still had to cross defended ground
evidence: Artillery-fortress syntheses identify low profiles and sloped or sunken works as core responses to direct fire.
limits: Lower was not invulnerable and surviving sites reflect later repairs as well as original plans.

artillery_problem: Round towers and straight curtains left dead ground near the wall
defensive_response: Project angled bastions so defenders could fire along neighboring faces
operational_effect: An attacker approaching one face could be exposed from another instead of sheltering beneath the wall
evidence: Parker describes bastions as gun platforms producing flanking and interlocking fields of fire; UNESCO identifies the bastioned system as an artillery response.
limits: Geometry shows intended fields of fire, not actual accuracy casualties or guaranteed defense.

artillery_problem: A single breached perimeter could turn bombardment into immediate assault
defensive_response: Add ditches ravelins and other outworks ahead of the main circuit
operational_effect: Besiegers first had to reach and reduce successive defended positions while exposed to fire
evidence: Parker describes outworks keeping guns and sappers farther from the main wall; the Venetian serial property preserves a network of evolving alla moderna works.
limits: Not every fortress contained every layer and added depth raised cost land use and garrison demands.
